title: Habitat
summary: A habitat is the natural home of a species - the specific place where it lives, feeds, and raises its young, with everything it needs to survive. Explore what makes a good habitat and why it matters.

crossReferences.label: Ecosystem (Ecology)
crossReferences.note: A habitat sits inside an ecosystem - it is the specific home of one species within the larger system.

crossReferences.label: Niche (Ecology)
crossReferences.note: The habitat is WHERE a species lives; the niche is its ROLE - the way it makes a living there.

compareCandidate.label: Habitat vs. niche
compareCandidate.description: The habitat is where a species lives - its address. The niche is its role - its job and lifestyle in that address, including what it eats and how it uses the space.

plainLanguageExplanation: A habitat is the natural home of a species - the place where it lives, finds food and water, gets shelter, and raises young. A fish's habitat might be a pond; a camel's habitat is the desert; a worm's habitat is the soil. A good habitat provides everything the organism needs: food, water, shelter, and the right space. If a habitat changes (like a forest being cut down), the organisms that live there can lose their home and may not survive. Each species has a preferred habitat, and protecting habitats is key to protecting species.

keyFacts.label: Definition
keyFacts.value: The natural home of a species

keyFacts.label: Provides
keyFacts.value: Food, water, shelter, and space to raise young

keyFacts.label: Examples
keyFacts.value: Pond for a fish, desert for a camel, soil for a worm

keyFacts.label: Change
keyFacts.value: A changed or lost habitat can threaten the species

keyFacts.label: Fit
keyFacts.value: Each species is adapted to its preferred habitat

keyFacts.label: Different from ecosystem
keyFacts.value: A habitat is one species' home; an ecosystem is the whole system

whyItMatters: Habitats are where life happens - every species has a place that meets its needs. Understanding habitats explains why animals live where they do and why protecting or losing a habitat changes everything for the species inside it.
didYouKnow: Polar bears and camels both live on Earth, but their habitats are as different as ice and sand - each is built for its own home.
